I made a post recently about how I suddenly lost my urge to smoke cigarettes, I decided to look back and see how long ago it was and it's been 7 days! I was thinking maybe more along the lines of like 3-4 days but it's just flown by. It's pretty crazy having been a daily smoker for the past 10 years or so and just dropping the habit overnight, I'm not sure what clicked but it's been really nice.

My lungs already feel cleaner and more healthy, I can breathe feeling more refreshed than before.. I do have bouts here and there where a cigarette sounds nice but then I actually think about it and it just goes away and I start feeling sick just thinking about smoking one. Maybe I'm just hitting the age where I realize how truly important it is to take care of my body and health if I want to live a good life.. whatever it is I'm thankful I grew the will to deny the cravings and hope I don't have a break in spirit in the future.

I'm sure the majority of people don't really care but I just thought I'd share, maybe even just to help motivate anyone else who's been thinking of quitting cigarettes too. It can be tough but at the same time it's possibly one of the easiest things to do, you just don't do it.

edit: you guys are so supportive, thank you :D

Congratulations to you, and you are going to enjoy the smoke-free things that happen to you: your breath will smell better, food will taste better and better and even more better as you go along. Showers will be more enjoyable and when you catch a cold, it will go away in half the time. You will soon smell things you missed for so long -- subtle scents like grass or rain or cooking.

I read a book about quitting smoking called 'The EASYWAY to Quit Smoking,' by Allan Carr and he questioned the craving for cigarettes in the following way: if you can sleep for eight to nine hours without needing a cigarette, then why would you ever need one? You will wake up if it is cold, or hot, if there is light or loud noises, if you need the bathroom or for anything else. So if you can sleep peacefully without a cigarette for 9 hours, why do you need them in your life?

As an obvious benefit as it may have been I'm really surprised at how much better my breath is.. it's like a night and day difference. Hell even if I forget to brush my teeth before going to bed my morning breath is still better than a day of casual smoking would've been.
